finding.claim: MUNIT formula function sizes a slice from an attacker-chosen dimension with no upper bound. A huge value panics the Go runtime (makeslice cap out of range), and the package has no recover(), so the calling process crashes. Moderate values (e.g. 1e5) allocate n*n formulaArg cells.
finding.source: Cell formula text in an untrusted .xlsx, e.g. <f>MUNIT(1E+18)</f>, parsed to a number at calc.go:5254 (ToNumber).
finding.sink: make([][]formulaArg, 0, int(dimension.Number)) at calc.go:5258 and the nested make/loop at calc.go:5259-5260.

finding.guards_checked: Argument-count check (5251); error/negative check (5255). No maximum dimension. No recover() anywhere in the package (grep found none). Precondition: caller invokes CalcCellValue/GetCalcCellValue on a workbook from an untrusted source.
finding.repro: Put =MUNIT(1E+18) in a cell of an .xlsx, open with excelize.OpenFile, call CalcCellValue on that cell. Expect a runtime panic (makeslice: cap out of range) that the library cannot recover. Derived from reading the code; not executed.

finding.claim: REPT formula function repeats the input string an attacker-chosen number of times with no output-length cap, so a large count exhausts memory and CPU. Excel's 32,767-character result limit is not enforced.

finding.claim: Zip size limits trust header-declared sizes, and the default total budget is about 16 GB. Non-worksheet parts are read fully into memory. A small, highly compressible .xlsx can therefore force a multi-GB heap allocation.
finding.source: Untrusted .xlsx bytes passed to excelize.OpenFile (excelize.go:134) or OpenReader (excelize.go:188). The attacker controls zip entry names, sizes and compressed content.
finding.sink: readFile (lib.go:157-166) reads every non-sheet, non-sharedStrings entry into memory via io.Copy into a bytes.Buffer. lib.go:162 pre-allocates make([]byte, 0, file.FileInfo().Size()) using the header-declared size.

ReadZipReader iterates all entries
fileSize taken from header
checkFileSize: per-entry and running-total check against UnzipSizeLimit
only sharedStrings above UnzipXMLSizeLimit is spilled to disk
only worksheets above UnzipXMLSizeLimit are spilled to disk
all other entries go to readFile in memory
buffer pre-sized to declared size
default UnzipSizeLimit = 1000<<24 (about 16.8 GB) from templates.go:195

finding.guards_checked: checkFileSize per-entry and total caps (lib.go:33-41); the disk spill for sheets and sharedStrings above UnzipXMLSizeLimit (lib.go:65, 74). Not guarded: in-memory path for other parts, and the up-front allocation sized by the header. Deflate can compress repetitive data about 1000:1, so a roughly 16 MB file can declare and expand to roughly 16 GB. Severity depends on the host and on whether the caller sets a lower UnzipSizeLimit.
finding.repro: Build an .xlsx whose xl/styles.xml (or any non-sheet part) is several GB of repeated bytes, deflate-compressed, so the file is a few MB to tens of MB. Call excelize.OpenFile with default options. Expect memory use proportional to the declared size. Not executed; derived from reading the code and the default limits.
